chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about an eye whose owner claims that he cannot see. He said: “He is to be given a delay of one year, then after the year he is to be made to swear that he does not see, then he is to be given the diyah.”
He said: I said, “Then if he sees after that?” He said: “It is something Allah has given him.”

key_terms.أَبْصَرَ: regained sight or came to see
key_terms.الْعَيْنِ: the eye, the injured organ under legal consideration
key_terms.يَدَّعِي: claims or alleges in a legal context
key_terms.يُؤَجَّلُ: is granted a delay or deferment
key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُ: is made to swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person claims blindness in one eye and later regains sight?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a claim of loss of sight in an eye for the purpose of diyah. The claimant is given a year, then made to swear an oath if the blindness remains, after which the diyah is awarded; if sight later returns, that recovery is treated as a blessing granted by Allah.
